## What This Is

**If you filled in your Writing Style Codex, apply `framework-manifest.json` first, before anything else in this update.** Through v3.14.0 the update script would overwrite your codex with the blank template on a single `--apply`, without asking.

Two changes lead. The Writing Style Codex is now a seeded file, which is what it always said it was. And the two doctrine counters now share one records boundary, so the orphan counter stops offering dated records as retirement candidates. A third change retires a protocol: the Conduction Flywheel's work moves into the Quest itself.

## The Defect

The Writing Style Codex ships unfilled on purpose. Its own Refinements entry says: "Once you do, this file is yours. It stays out of upstream sync, and no update will overwrite it."

The update script disagreed. `framework-manifest.json` classes everything under `Council Chamber/Codices/Expression/**` as framework, and the seeded list never named the codex. So `se-update.mjs --check` offered your filled-in codex as a framework update, and `--apply` replaced it with the template:

```
Applying upstream version of: Council Chamber/Codices/Expression/Writing Style Codex.md
Applied. The file is now staged.
```

That output is from v3.14.0. This release changes the codex, so every installed vault would have seen it offered.

## The Fix

`Council Chamber/Codices/Expression/Writing Style Codex.md` joins the seeded list. Seeded paths are checked before framework patterns, so the codex is now listed under SEEDED changes and `--apply` refuses it:

```
Refused: "Council Chamber/Codices/Expression/Writing Style Codex.md" is a seeded file.
```

## If You Are Updating an Existing Vault

1. **Apply the manifest first:** `node "Council Chamber/scripts/se-update.mjs" --apply "Council Chamber/scripts/framework-manifest.json"`. If you edited your manifest, add the codex path to `classes.seeded.paths` by hand instead.
2. **Run `--check` again.** The Writing Style Codex now lists under SEEDED. If it still lists under FRAMEWORK, stop and check step 1.
3. **Add the new Output Rule to your codex by hand,** if you want it. The text is under "Accuracy to the lived detail" below.
4. Apply the rest as `--check` lists it.

If you already ran `--apply` on the codex and committed, your filled-in version is in git history: `git log -- "Council Chamber/Codices/Expression/Writing Style Codex.md"`, then `git show <commit>:"Council Chamber/Codices/Expression/Writing Style Codex.md"` from the commit before the apply.

## Two Counters, One Boundary

`doctrine-mass.mjs` measures whether your doctrine is growing. `doctrine-references.mjs` finds doctrine nothing links to. Both are meant to count the same population. Through v3.14.0 they did not: the mass counter left dated records out, and the orphan counter had no boundary at all, so every dated audit report showed up as an orphan and a candidate for retirement.

The boundary now lives in one module, `doctrine-records.mjs`, and both counters import it. A record is either a file under a folder named in `RECORD_DIRS` (ships empty) or a file with `doctrine: false` in its frontmatter. The one dated audit the template ships, `Public Publish Audit - 2026-03-09.md`, now carries the marker. Both counters report 90 on this release, the audit excluded from each. On v3.14.0, marking that audit would have dropped it from the mass count and left it in the orphan list.

If you customized either counter, apply the intent rather than the file: import `isRecordDir` and `isMarkedRecord` from `doctrine-records.mjs`, and in the orphan counter skip any artifact for which either returns true before it enters the registry. A record still counts as a referrer, because a link from it is a real link. `Doctrine Mass Baseline.md` is seeded, so update its pointer to `RECORD_DIRS` by hand if you want it accurate.

## The Test That Proves It

`doctrine-records-selftest.mjs` builds a throwaway vault with five doctrine files and one planted record, CRLF line endings included, and runs both counters on it as real processes. Both must fail on an empty root. Both must count five. The record must be excluded from both. Then it strips the boundary out of a copy of the orphan counter and requires that copy to disagree, which is how the test is known to watch the right lines. It runs in CI.

```sh
node "Council Chamber/scripts/doctrine-records-selftest.mjs"
```

## Also in This Release

### Ported from practice

- **Accuracy to the lived detail, a new Output Rule** in the Writing Style Codex: "Accuracy to the lived detail. Where a draft rounds a lived fact, put back what actually happened. When a draft states a time, a count, a duration or a superlative from the Sovereign's telling, render it as they lived it. Keep their "-ish" and their hedge on any claim they cannot verify. Never round for rhythm. The correction can run either way: a detail the Sovereign asks to soften stays soft. The rule is accuracy rather than maximum precision."
- **A fresh-eyes reviewer is constituted three ways,** in the Engineering Codex orchestration section: independent (a new agent call with zero build context), ruthless (a first pass returning "looks good" is a failed review) and specific (every finding carries a measured value and a location). The Engineering Codex is a user-class file, so add the paragraph by hand. It sits before "Stay inline when any of these hold".
- **Meta-Governance Audit findings carry a class grep,** a new Finding Format section: each finding names the search that shows whether a sibling file carries the same text. A fix is complete when its class grep returns only history. A finding that arrives as a path and a line tends to get fixed at that line while the same text survives next door.
- **The Autonomous Improvement Session stops scheduling a retired item.** Its menu catalog retired T1-3 (the anti-AI sweep on draft articles), but the skill still listed it in the Tier 1 list, the short-window cadence and the model-routing table. All three are gone.
- **The Manuscript Anti-AI Edit Pass reads the codex version** from the Anti-AI Writing Patterns Codex frontmatter. It hardcoded "v1.3, 115 entries", which goes stale the first time you add an entry.
- **The Playwright skill states what `run.js` actually does:** a 15000 ms timeout with `domcontentloaded`, body text capped at 8000 characters and up to 50 links. It told you to raise timeouts to 15 seconds, the value they already had.
- **Sovereign Tech Watch:** the watched repo `affaan-m/everything-claude-code` was renamed upstream to `affaan-m/ECC`. The row now names the new URL. The old one redirects.

## The Conduction Flywheel Retires Into the Quest

The Conduction Flywheel Protocol read a completed Quest's reflections and proposed updates to an Archetypal Governance Map. The ecosystem never shipped that map, and the Conduction Codex told you to update it at Quest archival. So the flywheel's first run had nowhere to write, and a completed Quest's reading had no home.

The reading now lives in the Quest. **New: Quest Progress Update step 7b.** When a Quest's status becomes `completed`, the skill reads its `Trifecta Reflection` and `Archetypal ROI` sections and writes one paragraph under `## Completion Reading` in the Quest itself, naming what the Conduction Codex asks for at completion: archetype activated, domain engaged, range expanded, stability strengthened, blend capacity improved, shadow integrated and the energetic return. A North Star bias line is added only when the same pattern has appeared in more than one completed Quest. If either reflection section is empty, the skill asks for it first.

The protocol moves to `Vault (Archive)/Council Chamber/Protocols/Flywheels/` with a `superseded-by` marker pointing at the skill. The Conduction Codex, the Flywheel Integration Standard, the Security Flywheel Protocol, `AGENTS.md` and `MODULES.md` now point at step 7b. Nothing active still names the flywheel or the map.

### If You Are Updating an Existing Vault

`--check` lists the protocol as renamed into the archive. Archived files are your own class, so the update script never moves one for you.

1. **Move the protocol yourself:** in Obsidian, drag `Council Chamber/Protocols/Flywheels/Conduction Flywheel Protocol.md` into `Vault (Archive)/Council Chamber/Protocols/Flywheels/`. If you created your own Archetypal Governance Map and use it, keep both and skip this section.
2. **Apply the framework files:** the Conduction Codex, the Flywheel Integration Standard, the Security Flywheel Protocol, `AGENTS.md`, `MODULES.md` and the Quest Progress Update skill. If you customized the skill, add step 7b by hand after step 7 using the paragraph above.
3. **Confirm nothing active still points at it:**

```sh
grep -rn "Conduction Flywheel" . --include=*.md | grep -v "Vault (Archive)" | grep -v ".github/"
```

## Verification

Run on a snapshot of this release with `SOVEREIGN_VAULT_ROOT` unset:

- Every step of `verify.yml`, 25 of 25, including the new `doctrine-records-selftest.mjs` (14 of 14, three runs).
- `se-update.mjs --apply` on the Writing Style Codex: applied on the v3.14.0 manifest, refused on this one.
- Both doctrine counters on this tree agree, one record excluded.
- No active file names the Conduction Flywheel or the Archetypal Governance Map. The same grep finds both inside the archived copy, so its zero is real.
